messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: HIGH - multiple backend services failing to start due to KMS signing timeouts (observed across prod and prod-canary). Alert threshold hit at 06:12 UTC. Paging on-call.
maya: I'm on it. seeing repeated errors in startup logs for the auth-service: `kms.Sign` calls returning 504 / client timeout. A subset of pods can't complete bootstrap because they wait on signing to fetch node credentials.
alex: Confirmed. Stack traces show `context deadline exceeded` from our KMS client. This started ~06:10 UTC and error rate spiked ~x20. Latency to kms.amazonaws.com up to 8s.
sam: Is this AWS KMS only or do we see GCP KMS too? Any correlation with a specific region/az?
maya: Only AWS KMS so far, primarily us-east-1 and us-east-2 endpoints. GCP KMS looks fine.
jess: Customer impact: onboarding jobs and any service that does signing on cold-start is failing. Some live inference requests still working (cached credentials path), but new worker startups are impacted. Opening incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1857654321
alex: Quick mitigation plan proposal:
- enable local cached-data-key fallback for auth-service (GenerateDataKey caching) so startup doesn't block on remote Sign.
- increase KMS client timeout to 15s and add exponential backoff jitter in the short term
- throttle concurrent startup attempts to reduce KMS burst traffic
- contact AWS support and create ticket
maya: experimenting with step 1 now: toggling auth-service to use data-key cache for the next deploy. Pushing a non-breaking config flag to rolling-deploy pool-1.
sam: Also recommend short circuit: if KMS returns repeated 5xx/timeout on startup, allow process to start in degraded mode and retry signing in background. Less user-visible outage.
alex: Putting a temporary rate-limit on our side for KMS Sign calls to 500 rps per account to avoid hammering. Adding token-bucket in runtime.
incidents-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-185765 (internal) - AWS support case: 1234567890. Notifying provider.
aws-support-bot: AWS Incident update: We are investigating elevated latencies to KMS in us-east-1. Relevant AWS status: https://status.aws.amazon.com/messages/12345 - no ETA yet.
maya: Applied config change to auth-service -> enabled local data-key cache. Rolling 50% to start. Monitoring.
[log snippet pasted]
```
auth-service[pid=2234] ERROR bootstrap: failed to sign node key: context deadline exceeded (attempt=1)
auth-service[pid=2235] WARN using cached data-key for 5 minutes
```
alex: After toggling cache and increasing timeouts, pod restarts reduced and boot failures are down ~80% in the last 8 minutes. Still seeing intermittent Sign timeouts for some control-plane flows.
sam: Can we reduce non-essential KMS traffic? For example, disable periodic key-rotation jobs for 1 hour.
jess: Yes, I've paused scheduled key-rotation and non-critical background re-encrypt jobs in prod. Will monitor impact.
maya: Handing off to alex for next shift. I'm available on call if needed. Taking notes and adding timeline to the incident doc.
alex: Taking over. Current state: major customer impact reduced due to cache fallback, but still elevated error rate for KMS Sign in us-east. I've opened high-priority support case and requested a deeper infrastructure check. Contact channel for AWS support: aws-support@aws (thread 1234567890).
incidents-bot: Handoff reminder: maya -> alex at 06:40 UTC. Pager counts: 3 pages, 1 on-call escalation.
alex: Longer-term followups (postmortem action items):
- implement persistent data-key cache (secure) for faster bootstraps
- add KMS provider fallbacks (e.g., cross-region KMS routing) for signing operations
- add synthetic checks that exercise sign path from each region
- document degraded-startup mode and feature flag
sam: I'll own the synthetic checks and alerting tune-up.
jess: I'll coordinate customer comms for affected customers and prepare FAQ for SRE-runbooks.
aws-support-bot: Update from AWS: We identified a software issue in our KMS control plane causing elevated latencies in us-east-1. Mitigation in progress; expected recovery window 30-60 minutes. Case 1234567890.
alex: Noted. We'll keep the cached key fallback and throttles in place until AWS confirms recovery. I'll set a follow-up check at +30m and update the incident doc.
maya: Leaving a final note: if AWS declares recovery, we need a safe roll-back plan to remove cache and restore normal semantics. Do not delete cached data-keys until all pods have confirmed successful re-sign call.
incidents-bot: Incident state set to "mitigated" at 07:05 UTC (temporary mitigations applied). Postmortem owner requested: sam.
alex: Thanks team. Postmortem template link: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/ -- will fill in timeline and impact estimates once AWS finalizes.
jess: I'll send an outbound update to customer success and the affected accounts with root cause = AWS KMS control plane latency, mitigation = local caching + throttling, ETA for full resolution = per AWS update.
[reactions: :thumbsup: from maya, :eyes: from sam]
